evidence.source: Rekor Systems press release, GlobeNewswire, October 7, 2025

evidence.source: Rekor Systems press release / Investing.com, May 4, 2026

evidence.claim: Q3 2025 record results: $14.2M revenue, 63.4% adjusted gross margin, $1.5M adjusted EBITDA loss (best in company history); Q4 2025 first-ever operating cash flow positive quarter
evidence.source: Rekor Systems Q3 2025 earnings, GlobeNewswire, November 13, 2025

evidence.claim: Texas DOT statewide blanket PO for Rekor Command (June 2025); early Rekor Discover deployments with Caltrans and TxDOT announced October 2025 — potential for statewide conversion in 2026
evidence.source: Rekor Systems press releases, GlobeNewswire, June and October 2025

evidence.claim: Going-concern opinion issued by CBIZ CPAs (FY2025 10-K, March 2026) — second consecutive going-concern flag; Marcum LLP (prior auditor) resigned April 2025; Q1 2026 cash $12.6M vs. ~$20M annualized burn
evidence.source: Rekor Systems 10-K FY2025 (SEC), March 31, 2026; auditor resignation 8-K, April 2025

evidence.claim: Q1 2026: $10.3M revenue (+12% YoY), 64% recurring mix; missed consensus revenue by 21% and EPS by 75%; shares outstanding 136.6M (up 173% from 2021 peak)
evidence.source: Rekor Systems Q1 2026 earnings (StockTitan), May 2026; MacroTrends share count history

evidence.claim: Flock Safety: $300M ARR (March 2025), 70% YoY growth, 2,500+ communities, 42 states, 2,000+ law enforcement agencies — primary ALPR competitor 12x Rekor's recurring revenue base

Washington SB 6002 (effective March 30, 2026): 21-day ALPR data retention limit, sensitive-location collection bans, immigration enforcement prohibition — first state ALPR privacy law; police temporarily paused LPR systems to comply
evidence.source: MRSC Washington / Civic IQ Blog, April 2026

what_could_weaken_view: Cash crisis before Georgia DaaS revenue ramps — $12.6M cash vs. ~$20M annualized burn implies 7-9 months runway; equity raise at $0.79/share would add 30-50M shares and destroy remaining per-share value

Q3 2025 63.4% margin was non-recurring — driven by high-margin perpetual license sales, not sustainable DaaS ramp; if Georgia deployment lags, Q4 2025 operating cash flow positivity does not repeat in 2026

Texas and California pilots do not convert to statewide contracts — early deployments are proofs of concept, not committed revenue; two states passing keeps Georgia as a single-data-point, not a replicable model

Flock Safety enters FHWA-compliant DOT traffic analytics — Flock has government relationships, ALPR infrastructure, and ample capital to build a competing Discover-style product and bid on DOT DaaS contracts

Privacy legislation cascades beyond Washington — additional state ALPR restrictions (data retention caps, sensitive-location bans) would compress the law enforcement ALPR segment that drives ~49% of recurring revenue
Two CEO changes in 10 months + auditor resignation + founder interim CEO = organizational instability; executive search for permanent CEO not yet complete as of Q1 2026
